title: Instrument Private installer audit events for install/upgrade/rollback (cluster + operator + package version)
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
body:
## Context
Enterprise/private customers have flagged installer-driven changes (install/upgrade/rollback) as “must-audit” actions for security reviews (who changed what, when, on which cluster, and to what version). Today, the private installer logs to stdout/files and (sometimes) posts status to the control plane, but we do not emit canonical schema-v1 audit events.

This ticket adds audit events for:
- Private deployment install
- Private deployment upgrade
- Private deployment rollback

Including:
- package version (and target version)
- operator identity (human actor) or service actor attribution
- cluster identifier (stable ID used across upgrades)

## Goals
- Emit schema v1 compliant audit events from the private installer / upgrade controller code paths.
- Ensure events are delivered reliably (buffer + retry) and appear in the private Audit Logs UI/API.
- Provide enough target details to answer “what changed” without leaking secrets.

## Non-goals
- Full historical backfill of legacy installer logs.
- Auditing every individual k8s resource change (we only audit the user-meaningful action).

## Proposed audit events (names per naming guidelines)
Primary events (one per action; include outcome + error semantics):
- private.installer.install
- private.installer.upgrade
- private.installer.rollback

Optional follow-ups (if we need a start/finish pair for long-running operations):
- private.installer.install.started / .completed
- private.installer.upgrade.started / .completed
- private.installer.rollback.started / .completed

Decision (pending Security/Telemetry): prefer single event with outcome=success|failure, plus duration_ms, unless we need a “started” event for UI progress. We can add started/completed later without breaking schema v1.

## Required fields (schema v1)
All events must include the v1 envelope fields (see ENG-2481):
- schema_version: 1
- event_name: as above
- occurred_at
- org: {org_id, workspace_id} if available in private control plane context
- actor: attribution rules below
- target: deployment/cluster info below
- request_id / trace_id: where applicable
- source: "redwood-private-installer" (service name) and installer build metadata
- ip + user_agent: only if the action is triggered via a UI/API request and those values exist upstream; do NOT attempt to infer client IP on-cluster
- outcome: success|failure
- error: only on failure (code + message sanitized)

## Actor attribution rules
We need consistent “operator identity” behavior across air-gapped + connected installs.

1) If installer is invoked via Console/API action (connected mode):
- actor.type = human
- actor.user_id = Redwood user id
- actor.email = email (if already present in identity context)
- actor.session_id (if present)
- actor.impersonated_by (if applicable)

2) If installer is invoked manually on a bastion/on-prem machine (no upstream identity):
- Require operator identity to be passed explicitly (new required flag): --operator-email (or --operator-id if we have stable IDs)
- actor.type = human
- actor.email = flag value
- actor.user_id = "external" (string literal) or omit (per schema guidance)

3) If initiated by automation (e.g., GitOps runner / scheduled controller):
- actor.type = service
- actor.service = "gitops" or "private-upgrade-controller" (as appropriate)
- actor.service_instance_id = pod uid / job id

If operator identity is missing in manual mode:
- Emit event with actor.type=unknown and outcome=failure (preferred) OR block execution with a clear error.
- Proposal: block execution for install/upgrade/rollback in GA builds; allow override via --allow-unknown-actor for breakglass only (and still emit an event).

## Target modeling (cluster/deployment)
Target should enable correlation across all installer actions:
- target.type = "private_cluster"
- target.cluster_id = stable cluster UUID (generated at install and persisted in /var/lib/redwood/cluster_id or k8s secret)
- target.deployment_id = control plane deployment id (if available)
- target.environment = prod|staging|dev (if known)

Include change payload (non-secret):
- action = install|upgrade|rollback
- package.name = redwood-private
- package.from_version (upgrade/rollback only)
- package.to_version (install/upgrade/rollback)
- package.channel = stable|beta|hotfix (if used)
- orchestration = helm|kustomize|operator (if meaningful)

## Redaction requirements
Do not log:
- license keys
- kubeconfigs
- tokens / bearer strings
- customer domain secrets

If we include a diff, it must be bounded and explicitly allowlisted (likely not needed for v1). Coordinate with redaction rules (PR: redwood/pr_18577).

## Implementation plan
1) Identify all code paths:
- fresh install command
- upgrade command
- rollback command
- partial failures (e.g., post-install health checks fail)

2) Add cluster_id persistence:
- Ensure cluster_id is generated once at install and persisted for future upgrades
- Ensure rollback uses same cluster_id

3) Add audit emit call sites using shared library:
- Use ENG-2482 shared audit emitter + local validation
- Ensure we only emit after we know from_version/to_version values

4) Delivery semantics:
- In connected mode: emit to private control plane audit ingest endpoint
- In disconnected mode: spool to disk and retry until ingest is reachable (bounded disk usage; rotate)

5) Testing:
- Unit tests: event payload validates against schema v1
- Integration: extend audit-log integration harness (ENG-2492/PR redwood/pr_18501) to cover private upgrade in a test env (may require a lighter-weight “installer dry-run” path)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For each of install/upgrade/rollback, an audit event is emitted on both success and failure.
- [ ] Each event includes: event_name, occurred_at, outcome, actor, target.cluster_id, package.to_version.
- [ ] Upgrade/rollback include package.from_version.
- [ ] Actor identity rules enforced:
  - connected mode uses console/API identity
  - manual mode requires --operator-email (or documented breakglass)
- [ ] Events pass schema validation locally (fail fast on invalid payload).
- [ ] No secrets are present in payload (verified via tests + redaction allowlist).
- [ ] Events are visible/queryable via private Audit Logs API/UI (once that API is wired in Private).

## Open questions
- Should we use started/completed event pairs for long-running upgrades? (Telemetry prefers single event; SRE is OK with either as long as outcome is explicit.)
- Where should cluster_id live (host filesystem vs k8s secret)? Proposal: both (file as source-of-truth, secret for easy access in-cluster).

## Links
- Audit schema v1 work: ENG-2481
- Shared emitter/validator: ENG-2482
- Naming guidelines: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/audit-event-naming-guidelines.json
- Program overview: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-program-overview.json

Related implementation PR (expected):
- github.com/redwood-private-installer PR: pr_611 ("Emit audit events for private install/upgrade/rollback operations")

## Updates
2025-06-03 (Bruno Silva):
- Confirmed installer has distinct code paths for install vs upgrade; rollback currently re-runs helm with pinned chart version.
- Added draft cluster_id generation + persistence; needs review re: host path permissions for on-prem.

2025-06-10 (Marcus Lin):
- Security asks we BLOCK manual upgrades without operator identity for GA builds. OK with breakglass flag gated behind explicit “I understand” prompt.
- Reminder: do not log kubeconfig context names (can include customer internal hostnames).

2025-06-17 (Nadia Rahman):
- Telemetry preference: single event with duration_ms; avoid started/completed for v1 unless UI needs it.
- Ensure we propagate request_id when the upgrade is triggered from Console; otherwise omit rather than invent.

2025-06-18 (Bruno Silva):
- Implemented event emission behind feature flag PRIVATE_AUDIT_EVENTS=1 for easier staging rollout.
- Next: wire spool-to-disk for disconnected mode + add schema validation failures to installer stderr with actionable message.
